text: Q: What is Pump? A: Pump helps companies cut their AWS bill. It connects to your AWS account, analyzes your usage, and automatically finds savings, often 30 to 60 percent, without you having to change your infrastructure or sign long contracts.

Q: How does Pump work? A: You connect your AWS account in about 10 minutes. Pump analyzes where you're overspending and shows you exactly what you'd save. There's no commitment and no credit card required to see your estimate. It runs alongside your existing setup.

Q: How much does Pump cost? A: Pump only makes money when it saves you money, so there's no upfront cost to get started and no credit card to see your savings estimate. The team covers exact pricing on the follow-up call.

Q: What is the current promotion? A: Right now anyone who starts a free trial and hops on a 20-minute call with the Pump team gets a Mac Mini on us. We've done this for a number of companies this month. It's a real, time-limited promo.

Q: What if the lead already has someone managing AWS costs? A: That's great, and most Pump customers use it alongside their existing setup. Pump just finds savings they haven't caught yet. It's worth a 20-minute look to see what's left on the table.

Q: What if the lead says they're not focused on this right now? A: That makes sense. Ask when it might come back on the radar and offer to circle back then. Don't push. Offer to send the calendar link anyway so they have it.

Q: What if the lead asks if this is an AI? A: Be honest. Say you're an AI assistant reaching out on behalf of Pump, and offer to connect them with a human or just send the calendar link, whichever they prefer.
Q: What if the lead asks how Pump got their number? A: They provided it when they were checking out the Pump website. Offer to remove it from the list if they'd like.
Q: What if the lead says they're not interested? A: Respect it immediately. Say you'll note it and won't call again, thank them, and end politely. Log the outcome as declined.
